title: Śivastotrāvalī — Garland of Hymns to Śiva
author: Utpaladeva
text:
The Śivastotrāvalī is Utpaladeva's great cycle of hymns — twenty stotras in our text — composed in tenth-century Kashmir and regarded as one of the high achievements of devotional poetry within the recognition school. Its stance is set early: love does not wait for method. The devotion it sings is rule-free and self-young, undawned by practice, unaged by delay; against the grain of system-building that its author also practiced, the garland lets praise rather than proof take the lead.

Its juice: here the metaphysics of recognition is transposed entirely into song. What Utpaladeva argues elsewhere in sūtra, the hymns enact as gratitude — and their juice is the discovery that the self's return to its Lord needs no intermediate steps, only the willingness to address it directly.
